###chapter 1
My fingers grip the steering wheel, slick with sweat. I kill the engine. The massive estate looms ahead, and my legs feel like lead as I step out. It’s over. Actually, officially over. The signed papers are heavy in my bag, a physical reminder of my freedom. I’m just here to drop off his copy and grab Asher. That’s it.

I slip through the front door. Low murmurs drift from the back of the house. I freeze right outside the kitchen, the air suddenly freezing in my lungs. 

"But why can't you just live with us?" Asher’s small voice cracks. "Me and Mom?"

I press a hand to my ribs, trying to hold my chest together. God, the hurt in his voice kills me. I’d die for my kid, but this split? It had to happen. We were a trainwreck from day one. A total, absolute mistake. I was just too blind to see it. 

"Hey, buddy," Declan says. His tone is incredibly gentle. "You know why. Your mom and I aren't a team anymore." 

It hits me like a slap. In nine years, he never used that voice with me. Not once. With me, he was always a brick wall. Cold. Dead.

"But why?" Asher presses. 

"Sometimes people just drift apart, kiddo," Declan mutters. 

I can picture his scowl. He’s trying to shut the kid down, shut the conversation down. But Asher has my DNA. He doesn't let things go. 

"Don't you love her anymore?"

My lungs lock up. I stumble back a step, my spine hitting the drywall. My pulse hammers in my ears. I wait, holding my breath. 

I already know the damn answer. The whole world knows it. He doesn't love me. Never did, never fucking will. It’s a brutal fact. Yet, some pathetic part of me still wants to hear what he says. Will he lie to protect our son, or just lay it out? 

A throat clears. Declan is squirming. "Asher..."

"Dad. Yes or no. Do you love Mom?" Asher’s voice is dead serious. 

A heavy sigh echoes in the kitchen. "I love her because she gave me you," Declan says. 

A cop-out. A total dodge. 

I squeeze my eyes shut, a wave of agony crashing over me. God, it still stings. Why did I expect anything else? He never said those words. Not at the altar. Not in the delivery room. Not even when we were tangled in the sheets, sweating and breathless. He kept his heart locked in a vault. I poured everything into him, and he paid me back in scars. Our marriage was a crowded bed. Me, him, and her ghost. The woman he’s been obsessed with for nearly a decade.

I swipe a tear away before it can fall. No more crying over a guy who treats me like trash. 

"Eavesdropping is pretty trashy, you know." 

His deep baritone snaps me out of it. I pull my shoulders back, plaster on a mask, and walk in. Declan is leaning against the marble island. My brand-new ex-husband. His grey eyes lock onto me, dripping with sarcasm.

I look at Asher. My whole world. The one perfect thing I got out of this mess. He’s got his dad’s killer bone structure and those piercing grey eyes, but my messy brown hair. 

"Hey, guys," I force a smile.

"Mommy!" Asher drops his crust, slides off the stool, and bolts into my arms, wrapping his arms around my waist. "I missed you so much."

"Missed you more, baby." I press a kiss to his forehead, and he scampers back to his lunch.

I shift my weight, feeling like a trespasser. This place used to be mine, but I’m a ghost here now. Honestly? I always was. He built this mansion for *her*. Every paint swatch, every tile—it was her dream, not mine. I should’ve known right then. He was never going to let her go. He was never going to love me back.

"Why are you here?" Declan checks his Rolex, his jaw tight. "We had a deal. No crashing my visitation."

"I know, I know," I say, holding up my hands. "The court finalized the papers today. I figured I'd drop off your copy when I came for Asher."

His face turns to granite. His mouth hardens into a flat line. That look always chips away at my soul. I’ve loved this man my entire life, and to him, I’m just an annoyance. He broke me, piece by piece, for years. And I let him. I kept hoping he’d wake up and love me. Stupid. 

I thought marriage would heal the lonely kid inside me. I thought I’d finally be wanted. What a joke. It was a living hell. I spent years competing with a ghost, a perfect memory I could never beat. 

I rub my sternum, trying to massage the ache away. It’s useless. Months apart, and it still fucking hurts.

"Asher, go upstairs," Declan orders, his teeth grit so tight his jaw muscles twitch. He spits out the word "mother" like it's poison. 

Asher looks at us, sensing the tension. "No yelling," he warns, pointing a finger before heading out.

The second the kid is gone, Declan slams his fist onto the marble. The bang echoes. His eyes are pure ice. 

"You have an office address, Lyra. You don't crash my time with my kid!" he snarls, fists clenched, looking ready to tear the kitchen apart.

"Declan, please—"

"No! Shut the fuck up! You ruined my life nine years ago. Then you pull this divorce stunt. What, is this your sick way of punishing me? Taking my kid because I didn't love you? Well, guess what? I fucking hate you."

He’s panting, chest heaving. His words hit like hollow-point bullets, tearing right through whatever was left of my heart. 

"I... I..." 

What do you even say to that? How do you answer the man you love telling you he hates your guts?

"Get the fuck out of my house," he spits. "I'll drop Asher off later."

I slide the papers onto the counter, my hands shaking. I open my mouth to apologize, but my phone buzzes in my purse. I pull it out. Screen reads: MOM.

I want to decline it, but she only calls when the world is ending. I swipe answer and press it to my ear. 

"Hey, Mo—"

"Hospital. Now. Your father's been shot!" she screams, hysterical, and the line goes dead.

The phone slips through my fingers, clattering onto the floor. I freeze, totally numb.

"What?" Declan's voice cuts through the fog.

My heart is hammering against my ribs. I scoop up the phone, staring at the blank screen. "My dad," I whisper. "He's been shot."

###chapter 2
"I gotta run. Can you watch Asher? No clue when I'll be back," I mumble, grabbing my purse off the counter. 

Declan's voice is a blur. "Yeah, sure. Let me call my mom to cover me, then I'm on my way." His words barely register over the high-pitched buzz screaming in my ears.

I kiss my kid goodbye, totally numb, and bolt. Next thing I know, I'm behind the wheel, gunning it toward the hospital. My brain immediately drifts back to the old days. Classic emotional neglect. I was the ghost child. Dad worshiped Aurora—she was his precious little princess. Mom lived for Corbin, her golden boy. Me? I was just Lyra. The leftover.

I spent my life feeling like a party crasher in my own home. Straight A's, track team, student council—didn't matter. I was always the outsider peeking through the window at their perfect little club. Then, nine years ago, the bomb dropped. Whatever tiny thread held us together snapped for good. Corbin iced me out. He and Dad treated me like literal trash, pretending I didn't exist. Mom only rang my phone if she had some grim announcement. And Aurora? Total radio silence for nine long years. Her parting gift to me: *You're dead to me. I don't have a sister.*

So now I'm speeding down the highway because someone put a bullet in my father. And my grand emotion? Nothing. Just blank space. Am I broken? Shouldn't I be crying? How do you process the news that your lifelong bully is bleeding out on a gurney? Is it messed up that I don't care? The headlights blur as the past washes over me. The sting of being cast aside never really fades. It defines me. I'm the girl who got dumped—first by her blood, then by her husband and his snobby family. Asher is the only soul on this planet who actually loves me.

I pull into the lot of the town's only major hospital. I kill the engine, step out, and let the chilly night air smack my face. I pull my shoulders back, take a massive breath, and march inside. 

I hit the reception desk. "Hey, I'm looking for Alistair. He came in with a gunshot wound." 

The nurse looks up. "You family?" 

"Yeah. He's my dad." 

She taps her keyboard, eyes scanning the screen. "Okay, he's in the ER, getting prepped for the OR. Head straight down that hall, hit the double doors at the end. Your family is waiting there." 

"Thanks."

I walk down the corridor, my chest thumping like a bass drum. *He'll pull through,* I mutter under my breath. *He's tough. He'll be back to his usual self in no time.* I don't love the guy, but I don't want him dead. He might treat me like dirt, but he's actually sweet to Asher, and honestly, that's enough for me. 

I shove the heavy doors open. Mom and Corbin are huddled in the waiting area. I lock my face into a neutral mask and walk over. 

"Hey. Mom. Corbin." 

They look up. Mom's eyes are swollen, and her blue sundress is smeared with dark red blood. Corbin's eyes are dry, but his jaw is clenched tight. He's playing the rock for her.

I slide into the plastic chair beside her. "What the hell happened? How is he?" 

That triggers a fresh wave of sobbing. 

"He was walking back from the convenience store," she chokes out. "Right in front of the house. Two shots. I called 911 right away. The doctors said one bullet hit his lung, the other his kidney. They're prepping him for surgery now." Her voice cracks. 

I nod, staring at her. I want to wrap my arms around her, but I know she'd just stiffen up. "Hey, look at me. Dad's tough as nails. He's going to make it." 

She doesn't even look at me. Just keeps sobbing into her hands.

A few minutes later, the double doors swing open. They're wheeling Dad out on a gurney, hooked up to a dozen tubes. Mom and Corbin bolt upright and rush the bed. I stay glued to my seat. Trust me, the last thing a dying Alistair wants to see is my face. He's probably wishing Aurora was here instead. 

I watch Mom weep over his chest. He reaches up, weakly brushing a tear from her cheek, but she's a mess. He whispers something to Corbin, who nods with a grim, determined look. Right before they wheel him toward the OR, Dad slips a folded piece of paper into Mom's hand. She loses it completely, sobbing harder. She plants a quick kiss on his forehead, and the nurses push him through the doors. Mom and Corbin slump back into their chairs. Nobody says a word. The agonizing wait begins.

I can't sit still. I pace the floor, sit down, stand right back up. I grab a tray of crappy hospital coffee that nobody touches. The tension in the room is suffocating. Two and a half hours drag by. Finally, a doctor in scrubs walks in. One look at his face tells me everything. Dad's gone. Mom gets the vibe instantly; she starts hyperventilating, making these weird hiccuping sounds. 

"His heart stopped," the doctor says, his voice flat and heavy. "We did everything we could, but we couldn't get him back. I'm so sorry." 

Mom lets out this raw, guttural shriek—like a wounded animal. Her knees buckle, but Corbin catches her, and they both collapse onto the linoleum floor, sobbing in a heap. 

Dad is dead. And I realize what that means. Aurora is coming home.

###chapter 3
I slumped into the freezing plastic hospital chair, forcing air in and out of my lungs. Mom was a wreck, totally inconsolable, just sobbing her eyes out. God, it killed me to see her like this. I get it, though. Losing your husband out of nowhere? That’s brutal.

My brain was still short-circuiting. I really thought he’d pull through. But nope. He’s gone, and honestly, I’m just numb. 

We fought like cats and dogs, and yeah, he despised me. But I still loved the guy. He was my dad. You don't just turn that off.

"Hey. You holding up?" Declan slid into the seat next to me. 

He’d been here an hour, but this was the first time he’d even looked my way. The sudden worry in his voice threw me off. Since when did he give a crap about how I felt?

"Yeah," I muttered. 

Not a single tear had dropped since the doctor gave us the bad news. Maybe I was frozen, or maybe I just didn't have any tears left for him. Either way, I had to keep it together while everyone else was losing their minds.

A pair of shoes stopped in front of me. I looked up. Corbin. His eyes were dead, ice-cold, same as always. Look, I know I screwed up. But damn, haven't I paid my dues for that night already?

"What do you want?" I snapped.

"Mom buzzed Aurora right after Dad got shot," he said, his voice flat. "She's on her way. She doesn't know he didn't make it yet."

Beside me, Declan gasped. Just like that, I knew her name still wrecked him. The tiny bit of warmth he’d just given me evaporated. Gone. I’d lost him again.

"Figures," I mumbled. What else could I say? 

We hadn't talked in forever. She hated my guts anyway, so she probably wouldn't even want to breathe the same air as me.

"Play nice and stay out of her way," Mom chimed in, dabbing her wet cheeks.

"Mom, seriously? You're asking for a miracle here."

"I don't care," she hissed, jaw tight. "You chased my daughter away nine years ago when you stabbed her in the back. I won't let you ruin this. Not now. Not when your father is dead and we actually need to stick together."

God, I hated how they kept dragging up the past. I was young and stupid. Haven't I suffered enough for those mistakes? But no, the punishment never ends.

"Just so we're clear, I'm your kid too. Or did I die today as well?" 

I didn't wait for her to snap back. I bolted. I needed out. I needed to breathe and clear my head.

The freezing night air hit my face outside. My eyes burned, but I blinked the tears back. Why the hell was I even here? Why bother calling me if she only cares about her golden child?

A huge part of me wanted to just walk to my car and drive away forever. I never fit into their perfect little world anyway, and they made sure I knew it. I should just ghost them. They'd already forgotten about me, so why not?

"Excuse me, are you Alistair's daughter?" A nurse popped out of nowhere, scaring the absolute crap out of me.

I took a second to calm my racing heart, then nodded.

"They need you inside. For the viewing," she said gently, trying to soften the blow.

"Okay. Just... give me a sec." 

She walked off, leaving me to make my choice. Sure, he ignored me, but he paid the bills. I owed him that much. Fine. I'd help bury him, and then I was done. Out. They could have their picture-perfect family. No more dealing with the black sheep.

I headed back inside and got directions to the morgue. By the time I found it, the others had already said their goodbyes.

I stared down at him on the cold metal slab. He looked peaceful, honestly. Just like he was taking a nap. You'd think he was just sleeping. But he wasn't. He was gone. Just an empty shell.

"Bye, Dad," I whispered. 

I took one last look, then walked out of the freezing room. My chest felt heavy, but I shook it off. He wasn't the only one I was leaving behind today. They were never going to love me. Time to stop dreaming.

Back in the waiting room, I grabbed a chair in the far corner. Mom was busy shuffling paperwork and hospital bills. Corbin was staring blankly at the wall, totally checked out. Declan was gone.

I sat there, mapping out my next moves. Avoiding them would be a nightmare, but I had to do it. It was the only way to save my own sanity. I was done hurting. Done letting these people rip my heart out over and over.

A sudden noise made me look up. And there she was. God, she was still gorgeous. Long blonde hair, legs for days, that perfect heart-shaped face, and a killer body that made every guy in the room drool.

Corbin threw his arms around her, whispering sweet things in her ear. He hadn't even hugged me when I got here. That familiar sting of jealousy and hurt flared up, but I shoved it right back down.

They pulled apart just as Declan walked in. The second he spotted her, he literally stumbled. His throat tightened, his Adam's apple bobbing hard.

"Aurora?" he choked out. He packed a lifetime of pain and love into that one word. 

Her head snapped toward him. When their eyes locked, the rest of the room just vanished. It was just them. Then, faster than lightning, they crashed into a hug.

If Corbin's hug stung, this absolutely wrecked me. It ripped me to shreds. 

Aurora was back. And watching her wrap herself around Declan, I didn't need a map to see the obvious. He was still head over heels for her. Even after all this time.

###chapter 4
My chest feels like a garbage disposal switched on high, grinding my heart to mush. Seriously, if I could just reach in, yank the damn thing out, and toss it in the trash, I would. Anything to stop this agonizing burn. I want to bolt. I want to look away. But my eyes won't budge. They're locked onto the two of them, glued to the perfect little picture they're making.

They pull apart, slow. Declan's face goes all soft—that look he only has for his absolute favorite person. He cups her cheeks, pulling her in close. No kiss. Just forehead to forehead. He looks so damn peaceful. Like he finally made it back home. Like he's whole again. His lips move. *I've missed you.* I read the words clear as day.

What if they'd met like this while we were still married? Would he have cheated? Part of me wants to say no way, but who am I kidding? This is Aurora. Declan would literally walk through fire for her.

I can't take another second. I spin around and bolt outside. 

The second the cold air hits my face, I boil over. Tears just start spilling. God, it hurts. It hurts so bad and I have no clue how to turn the pain off. But hey, who's to blame here? Me. I'm the idiot who fell for a guy who was never mine to begin with.

"Please," I whisper to the empty sky. "Just make it stop. Please." 

Nothing. No magic fix. No relief. My hands fly to my collarbone. My lungs are squeezing shut. I'm gasping, trying to suck in air, but nothing's coming. It feels like I'm literally fading out. Dying, inch by inch.

"That's what you get for chasing a guy who isn't yours." Corbin's voice cuts right through my panic. 

"What do you want, Corbin?" I snap, wiping my face and throwing my walls right back up. "If you're just here to gloat or tell me to stay away from your precious sister, save it. Go back to the hospital with the rest of your family. You've got nothing to say to me."

He blinks, totally thrown off. Guess he didn't expect me to bite back. 

"Look, I'm just making sure you get the memo," he says, crossing his arms. "Declan was always Aurora's. You got greedy and stole him, but now they're back on track. Just don't mess this up for them. They've waited long enough."

I let out a sharp, ugly laugh. 

"Oh, don't worry. I'm done playing roadblock. After today, none of you ever have to look at my face again." 

He frowns, his eyebrows knitting together. "Wait, what's that supposed to mean?"

I'm too exhausted for this. I just want to crawl into bed, cry myself to sleep, and pretend today never existed. 

"Tell Mom I'll help with the funeral stuff—if she even wants me there. And tell your sister I said hi." 

I turn on my heel and march toward my car. Corbin yells my name, but I don't even pause. I just want to get home and fall apart in private. 

I hop in the driver's seat and hit the gas. Declan said Asher was staying with his mom. Good. I can't handle another person who despises my existence today. He's safe there, so I'll just grab him tomorrow. I make it home in record time. But stepping into the quiet house just hits me with how incredibly alone I am. No shoulder to cry on. No one waiting up. Nobody loves me. It's just me and Asher against the world.

The waterworks start up again. I'm so sick of crying, but the tears won't stop. If I could just build a time machine and fix my mistakes, maybe I'd be married to someone who actually gives a damn about me. But yeah, that's the past for you. Once it's done, it's set in stone.

Three days pass. Dad's death has everyone spiraling. It was so sudden, and since he was such a big deal around here, the whole town is reeling. I haven't seen Declan once. He's blown up my phone, sure, but I ignored every single call. He's probably wrapped up in Aurora's arms anyway. She's probably already moved her stuff into his place. I don't need him rubbing my nose in it.

I shake my head to clear the venom and struggle with the zipper of my black dress. 

"Mommy?" Asher's little voice pipes up behind me. 

I turn around. His eyes are swimming with tears. I drop to my knees so we're eye-to-eye. 

"Hey, baby, what's wrong?" 

"I miss him," he whimpers, his voice cracking. "We were supposed to go fishing this Saturday." 

My heart literally snaps. Alistair was a crappy excuse for a father to me, but he was a damn good grandpa to my kid. I pull Asher tight against my chest, whispering nonsense into his hair while his tears soak right through my shoulder.

"I know, sweetie. I know you miss him. But he's with the angels now, watching over you. And he's never really gone, because he's right here," I say, tapping his chest, "and right here," I touch his forehead. "Plus, he wouldn't want you crying. We don't want to make him sad, right?" 

He shakes his head, sniffing.

"Good. So here's the plan. Instead of crying, we're going to talk about all the awesome times you had with him, okay?" 

I don't have many good memories of my own, but Asher has tons. I'm going to make sure he holds onto them. 

"Okay," he whispers. 

I wipe his cheeks, grab my purse, and hold out my hand. He takes it, looking up at me. 

"Alright. Let's go say a proper goodbye to Grandpa." 

He gives me a tiny, brave smile, and we head out the door. Time to face the music.

###chapter 5
The weather was gorgeous. Total bait-and-switch. I cruised down the usual streets, thinking today would be just fine. Boy, was I wrong.

We pulled up to a packed house. The chapel was overflowing with people showing up for the final send-off.

I scanned the room. Everything looked perfect. Figures. The rest of the family didn't lift a finger for the funeral prep. The whole damn circus fell on my shoulders.

But hey, no complaints from me. It was my turn to pay him back. The man kept me fed, dressed, and gave me a roof when I had nothing.

People were sliding into pews. Showtime. I headed straight for the far side of the aisle. No way was I sitting with the main crew. And sitting next to Aurora? Yeah, hard pass.

"Hey, Mom," Asher whispered, tugging my sleeve and pointing across the aisle. "Why are we over here? Aren't we sitting with Grandma?"

Side-eyes started coming our way. Let them look. Everyone knew the family treated me like a black sheep after the whole mess anyway.

"Pews are full, bud. I don't want to make a scene," I lied.

He gave me that look but dropped it. The priest walked up, the sermon kicked off, and right then, a body slid onto the bench right beside me.

My muscles locked up. That cologne. I'd know it in my sleep. What the hell was he doing here? He belonged over there with his precious Aurora. Honestly, I wished he'd just go back to her.

God, I sounded so bitter. But I was. Mad, hurt, and totally pissed off.

"Dad!" Asher hissed-whispered. A couple of heads snapped toward us.

I shot them a death glare until they minded their own business.

"Hey, can I sit in the middle?" Asher whispered.

Thank God. A tiny miracle. Now I didn't have to choke on his heavy, suffocating vibe.

I quickly shuffled us around, putting Asher between us. Instantly, the air got a little easier to breathe.

"We're all going to die," the preacher droned from the pulpit. "But how will you go? Did you make an impact? Did you touch lives, or are you leaving behind a trail of regrets?"

The words hit home. If I kicked the bucket today, who'd show up? Would anyone even give a shit? Who was I kidding? Nope. They'd probably throw a party. Asher was the only one who'd actually cry. Just my boy. No one else.

It was a pathetic existence, really. Zero friends because I kept my walls up. Growing up in Aurora's perfect shadow meant I was never enough. I wasn't the hot one. Or the smart one. Or the loved one. Aurora was flawless. I was just... background noise.

Years later, nothing had changed. Still in her shadow. Nobody cared about my struggles. It was always the Aurora Show. Her heartbreak was more tragic. Her joy was more important. She got the spotlight; I got the scraps of love they threw on the floor.

"Mom?" Asher's voice snapped me back to reality.

I blinked. The service was done. People were already shuffling out.

"Lyra, you good?" That deep voice of his sent a shiver straight down my spine.

I didn't want to look at him, let alone talk. But we had ten more years of co-parenting ahead. I had to play nice.

I shrugged, stood up, and kept my eyes glued to the floor. Rude? Maybe. But I couldn't look at him. Not with the mental image of him staring adoringly at Aurora burned into my brain.

"Let's go, Asher. Move it."

He hopped up, and we headed for the exit. Outside, the crowd swarmed us with the usual condolences. I spotted a few coworkers in the mix and gave them a weak wave.

We hadn't even put Dad in the ground yet, and I was already running on empty.

"Look who finally decided to show up," Aurora's venomous voice hissed from behind.

I turned around. Even with puffy eyes and a blotchy face, she still looked like a damn supermodel.

I let out a heavy sigh. I really didn't have the energy for this.

"Not now, Aurora. Can we just get through the burial first?"

She smirked, leaning close so her words were for my ears only.

"Oh, we'll bury him. But get this—I'm not going anywhere. You stole my family back then, but game over. I'm taking back what's mine. Everything. Including the guy who was always supposed to be with me." She backed off and walked away just as the preacher waved us toward the gravesite.

Asher looked from me to her retreating back, staying quiet. I stood there, stunned but not shocked. Classic Aurora.

What she didn't get was that there was nothing to steal. None of it was ever mine. The family worshipped her. And Declan? Please. He was always hers, anyway.

I swallowed the lump in my throat and guided Asher toward the open grave.

I kept my distance from Mom, Aurora, and Corbin. They were all huddled up. To anyone else, I looked like a random guest, not family.

"Ashes to ashes, dust to dust..." the preacher intoned as the casket went down.

Dirt started hitting the wood. Mom lost it, screaming for him to come back. Aurora and Corbin just sobbed quietly, holding her tight.

I pulled Asher close, holding him while he sobbed. Seeing him hurt broke me. I blinked back my own tears. No, I had to be the strong one. He needed me.

More fake smiles and handshakes. I went on autopilot, totally zoning out. By the time I snapped back, the crowd had mostly cleared.

"Mom, look, Grandma and Grandpa," Asher said, pulling my arm toward Declan's parents.

They were standing with Declan and his twin, Orion.

I stood there like an idiot while Asher ran over. They gave me a cold glance but said nothing. No surprise there—they never wanted me for their son.

"Can I go grab snacks with them?" Asher asked. I nodded.

The kid was starving anyway. Once they walked off, Declan and I were left in awkward silence. With Asher gone, his eyes immediately drifted back to Aurora, who was standing just a few yards away.

I opened my mouth to leave, but then—*screeech*. Tires squealed. Everything went sideways in a second. Gunmen. Shots fired. And the instant the bullets flew, Declan dove straight for Aurora.

I froze, watching him shield her with his own body.

He left me to die to save her. Why was I even shocked? It was the ultimate proof: I was never going to be his number one. Watching him play hero for her broke whatever was left of my heart.

"Get down!" a guy in a tactical vest screamed.

He shoved me hard, but too slow. A sharp, hot pain ripped through me. I hit the dirt, the wind knocked right out of my lungs.

"We need a medic! Now!" the guy yelled, kneeling and slamming his hands over my wound.

My head spun. Everything hurt. I tried to say I was fine, but then I saw the red soaking my dress and his hands. God, I hated blood.

"Oh God... Asher," I choked out.

He was my very last thought before the world went completely black.

###chapter 6
Watching your ex-wife—the woman who gave you your son—bleeding out on the freezing dirt of a graveyard does something to your head. It triggered a raw, twisted knot in my chest I never thought I’d feel for Lyra.

The second those barrels lined up on us, my brain went totally blank. Asher was safe at my folks' place, so my body just reacted. I threw myself over Aurora. I was ready to take a bullet for her. Simple as that.

The shooters bolted when the sirens wailed, and I breathed a quick sigh of relief. Then a cop screamed for a medic, and that relief vanished. I spun around, scanning the ground to see who got hit. When I saw Lyra down, my knees turned to water.

Everything after that was a blur of flashing lights. The paramedics rolled up, but the cop on scene wouldn't step back until he personally saw the ER doc take over her gurney.

The guy’s hesitation pissed me off—she was my wife. Well, ex-wife. But the real anger was aimed right at myself. I was supposed to keep her safe. If she died today, what the hell was I going to tell Asher? How do you tell your kid you let his mother get shot?

Now, I was wearing a groove into the waiting room floor. Pacing, sweating, losing my mind. They’d wheeled her into the trauma bay hours ago and we hadn't heard a damn thing. No updates. No doctor. Nothing.

###chapter 7
My back is stiff as hell, and my arm is throbbing. Asher is right next to me, fast asleep. The kid refused to budge after the TV went black last night. I can't help but smirk, remembering his little speech. *I'm on duty,* he’d said, dead serious about keeping me safe all night.

I wiggle out from under him, trying not to jar my bad side. It takes some doing, but he doesn't stir. I glance at the clock. Eight. Time to get some food going before he opens his eyes.

I do a quick bathroom run, head downstairs, and freeze right outside the kitchen. I stare at the counter. How the hell am I supposed to whip up breakfast with only one working hand?
